newsitem.title: VIETNAM: First U.S. envoy to Hanoi clears ceremonial hurdle.
newsitem.headline: First U.S. envoy to Hanoi clears ceremonial hurdle.

text.p: The United States' first ambassador to post-war Vietnam began a round of protocol meetings in Hanoi on Wednesday, presenting his credentials to Vice-President Nguyen Thi Binh.
Douglas "Pete" Peterson, a fighter pilot and prisoner of war in the conflict which ended 22 years ago, was greeted with little ceremony when he walked across the tarmac at Hanoi airport last week.
But the red carpet was rolled out and honour guards stood to attention at the grand, French-built presidential palace on Wednesday for his meeting with Binh.
The 61-year-old former congressman presented the vice-president with an introduction from U.S. President Bill Clinton and then stood with officials from both sides while cameras clicked and whirred.
Behind them was a giant bust of Ho Chi Minh, the revered revolutionary and founding father of communist Vietnam.
Peterson then met privately with Binh for about 30 minutes before leaving, ignoring journalists' shouted questions.
The appointment of the first U.S. ambassador to Hanoi comes two years after the former foes normalised diplomatic ties and was delayed because of political and legal obstacles.
Peterson proclaimed a new era in relations on arrival in Vietnam last week and spoke of an opportunity for the two countries to bury their history of conflict and suspicion.
"In time, I am confident that we will not think of ourselves as former adversaries, but as very good friends," he said.
